content: The text provided appears to be a long list of references from various studies, articles, and systematic reviews related to home safety, injury prevention, fall prevention, and associated risk factors in different populations, including children, the elderly, and individuals with disabilities. 1. LeBlanc JC and colleagues conducted a multicenter case-control study to evaluate the effectiveness of home safety measures in reducing the risk of unintentional injuries among young children. (CMAJ, 2006) 2. A study published in 2010 explored the relationship between home hazards and the risk of falls among community-dwelling seniors who utilize home-care services. (Rev Epidemiol Sante Publique, 2010) 3. Chronic Disease Canada (2008) presented an extended hazards model incorporating time-dependent covariates to identify risk factors for falls among seniors receiving home-care services. 4. A randomized controlled trial published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society (2007) assessed the impact of fall prevention programs on the quality of life in older adults who had experienced falls. 5. Loder RT analyzed the demographics of playground equipment-related injuries in children, highlighting the prevalence and patterns of such injuries. (J Pediatr Surg, 2008) 6. A randomized controlled trial published in BMJ (2010) evaluated community-based fall prevention interventions for individuals who called emergency services after a fall. 7. Lok N and Akin B identified domestic environmental risk factors associated with falls in elderly populations, as reported in the Iran Journal of Public Health (2013). 8. Lu Z and colleagues investigated how the physical environment influences walking behaviors among assisted living residents, based on findings from focus group discussions. (J Appl Gerontol, 2011) 9. Lyons RA et al. examined the association between specific built forms in homes and the occurrence of injuries, as published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine (2006). 10. MacDougall FJ and colleagues developed an early childhood burn and scald prevention program, Too Hot for Tots, as a tool for community educators. (J Burn Care Res, 2013) 11. Malta DC et al. analyzed the characteristics and factors contributing to emergency service visits for falls, as reported in Rev Saude Publica (2012). 12. Manrique-Espinoza B and colleagues studied the prevalence of falls and fractures among elderly individuals living in extreme poverty conditions. (Inj Prev, 2010) 13. A cross-sectional study in the Canadian Journal on Aging (2010) examined the prevalence, correlates, and costs of falls among older home-care clients at risk of falling. 14. Mashreky SR et al. conducted a nested case-control study to identify determinants of childhood burns in rural Bangladesh. (Health Policy, 2010) 15. Meadows-Oliver M discussed the importance of window safety devices in preventing injuries among children. (J Pediatr Health Care, 2010) 16. Michael YL and colleagues provided an updated systematic review of interventions aimed at preventing falls in older adults. (Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, 2010) 17. A Japanese prospective cohort study published in the Journal of Gerontological Nursing (2014) explored the role of home modifications in preventing frailty progression in older adults. 18. Mitty E and Flores S outlined assessment strategies and interventions for fall prevention in assisted living facilities. (Geriatr Nurs, 2007) 19. A study in the Australian Journal of Physiotherapy (2004) identified predisposing factors for occasional and multiple falls among older Australians living at home. 20. Mueller BA et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the functionality of ionization and photoelectric smoke alarms. (Inj Prev, 2008) 21. Mulvaney C and Kendrick D examined engagement in safety practices to prevent home injuries among preschool children in white and non-white ethnic minority families. (Inj Prev, 2004) 22. Myers RP et al. investigated the risk of sustaining burns from household heating pads, identifying vulnerable populations. (J Burn Care Res, 2012) 23. Nachreiner NM and colleagues studied the circumstances and consequences of falls among community-dwelling older women. (J Women’s Health, 2007) 24. The National Safety Council published Injury Facts in 2003, providing comprehensive data on injury patterns and prevention strategies. 25. A prospective cohort study examined wheelchair-related falls among veterans with spinal cord injuries living in the community. (Arch Phys Med Rehabil, 2010) 26. Neyens JC et al. systematically reviewed the effectiveness of interventions for preventing falls in elderly individuals residing in long-term care facilities. (J Am Med Dir Assoc, 2011) 27. Olaitan P and Dairo M analyzed domestic fire accidents in a developing country and proposed modifications to reduce morbidity and mortality. (Internet J Rescue Disaster Med, 2006) 28. Osborne JM et al. explored the role of home environments in child injury prevention, focusing on fall risks and fractures. (Clin Calcium, 2013) 29. A case-control study in the Journal of Injury Prevention (2013) identified risk factors for burns at home among Kurdish preschool children. 30. Parker EM et al. investigated fire and scald burn risks in urban communities, identifying at-risk populations and their beliefs about home safety. (Health Educ Res, 2013) 31. Park-Lee E and Sengupta M analyzed falls among cognitively impaired residents in assisted living facilities, based on findings from the 2010 National Survey of Residential Care Facilities. 32. Pearce A et al. examined the influence of home environments on inequalities in unintentional injuries during early childhood, using data from the UK Millennium Cohort Study. (J Epidemiol Community Health, 2012) 33. Pearson M et al. systematically reviewed the effectiveness of programs supplying and installing home safety equipment to prevent unintentional injuries in children. (Health Promot Int, 2011) 34. Pereira SG et al. studied the prevalence of household falls among long-lived adults and their association with extrinsic factors. (Rev Latino-Am Enfermagem, 2017) 35. Phillips CJ et al. conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of introducing bath thermostatic mixer valves in social housing to prevent bathwater scalds. (Inj Prev, 2011) 36. Pighills AC et al. evaluated environmental assessment and modification strategies to prevent falls in older adults. (JAGS, 2011) 37. Polzien G emphasized promoting safety and security at home through home healthcare interventions. (Home Healthc Nurse, 2007) 38. Powell EC et al. conducted a randomized trial of a home safety education intervention using a safe home model. (J Trauma, 2010) 39. Pressley JC and Barlow B analyzed child and adolescent injuries resulting from falls from buildings and structures. (Inj Prev, 2005) 40. Pressley JC et al. examined racial and ethnic differences in home safety practices using vouchers for free safety devices. (J Trauma, 2009) 41. Qiu X et al. identified predictors of home injury hazards among toddlers in Wenzhou, China, through a community-based cross-sectional study. (BMC Public Health, 2014) 42. Ranawera AD et al. studied the incidence and risk factors of falls among the elderly in Colombo District. (Ceylon Med J, 2013) 43. Ravindran RM and Kutty VR identified risk factors for fall-related injuries leading to hospitalization among community-dwelling older persons in Kerala, India. (Asia Pac J Public Health, 2016) 44. A systematic review published in the Lancet (2015) highlighted the role of home safety modifications in reducing injuries from falls. 45. Rubenstein LZ et al. developed quality indicators for managing and preventing falls and mobility problems in vulnerable elders. (Ann Int Med, 2001) 46. Runyan CW et al. analyzed unintentional injuries in the home in the United States, focusing on morbidity patterns. (Am J Prev Med, 2005) 47. A study in Age and Ageing (2012) evaluated the economic impact of community falls prevention programs alongside a randomized controlled trial. 48. Sadeghi-Bazargani H et al. identified household-related predictors of burn injuries in an Iranian population through a case-control study. (BMC Public Health, 2012) 49. Sahiner P et al. investigated the incidence and risk factors of home accidents in low socioeconomic households in Kocaeli. (TAF Prev Med Bull, 2011) 50. Schlisman CA discussed fall risk reduction strategies in home healthcare and hospice settings. (Home Healthc Nurse, 2008) 51. Schwebel DC et al. examined the physical environment of homes and its impact on adolescent injury risk. (Int Emerg Nurs, 2009) 52. Scott V et al. reviewed strategies for preventing falls and related injuries among seniors in assisted living residences. (Inj Prev, 2010) 53. Shai D analyzed the relationship between income, housing, and fire injuries using census tract data. (Public Health Rep, 2006) 54. Shin KR et al. evaluated the effects of a fall prevention program on knowledge, self-efficacy, and preventive activities among low-income elderly women. (Taehan Kanho Hakhoe Chi, 2005) 55. Sjostena NM et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial of a multifactorial fall prevention program for home-dwelling elderly individuals. (Public Health, 2007) 56. Somrongthong R et al. explored the effects of housing on health and health risks in an aging population in rural Thailand. (Biomed Res Int, 2014) 57. Sophonratanapokin B et al. studied the impact of living environments on falls among the elderly in Thailand. (Southeast Asian J Trop Med Public Health, 2012) 58. Stefanacci RG and Haimowitz D emphasized the importance of fall prevention strategies in geriatric nursing. (Geriatric Nursing, 2012) 59. Stolze H et al. reviewed the prevalence, risk factors, and etiology of falls in common neurological diseases. (J Neurol, 2004) 60. Stewart J et al. identified modifiable risk factors for scald injuries in children under five years of age through a multicenter case-control study. (Burns, 2016) 61. Teems J et al. reported increased preventive behaviors for falls and fractures among older adults following a community-based intervention. (J Nutr Gerontol Geriatr, 2011) 62. Terschueren C et al. presented initial results of individual fall prevention interventions by trained nurses in private homes of older adults. (Poster Abstract, 2006) 63. Turner S et al. demonstrated that installing home safety devices reduces the incidence of preventable injuries in young children. (J Pediatrics, 2011) 64. Unwin BK et al. discussed therapeutic home adaptations for older adults with disabilities. (Am Fam Physician, 2009) 65. Valenza T highlighted the importance of home modifications in rehabilitation management. (Rehab Management, 2007) 66. Vish NL et al. analyzed pediatric window falls, emphasizing that this issue is not limited to children in high-rise buildings. (Inj Prev, 2005) 67. Vladutiu CJ et al. examined the relationship between disability, home hazards, and safety practices in U.S. households. (Disabil Health J, 2012) 68. Watson DS et al. studied injuries related to trimming and pruning activities in the United States from 1990 to 2007. (J Trauma Acute Care Surg, 2012) 69. Webb-Henderson S et al. discussed strategies for reducing fall risks in the home. (Caring, 2009) 70. Wing JJ et al. investigated the role of environmental factors in falls among stroke survivors. (Arch Gerontol Geriatr, 2017) 71. The World Health Organization and UNICEF published the World Report on Child Injury Prevention in 2008, emphasizing strategies to keep children safe at home. 72. Yeh ES et al. analyzed injuries associated with cribs, playpens, and bassinets among young children in the U.S. (Pediatrics, 2011) 73. Zhang G et al. studied fire safety among the elderly in Western Australia.
